Storm Damage Lead Generation Strategies for Roofing Companies

Proven storm damage lead generation strategies for roofing companies. Includes pre-storm prep, emergency PPC, insurance relationships, and post-storm campaigns.

Storm damage creates one of the most concentrated buying windows in home services. When hail pounds a neighborhood or a tornado tears through a county, thousands of homeowners suddenly need roofing work done immediately. The contractors who capture those leads in the first 48 to 72 hours often book months of work. The ones who wait for the phone to ring watch their competitors sign every profitable job in the area.

This guide covers storm damage lead generation from every angle: what to do before storm season starts, how to operate during an active event, and how to convert the surge of interest into long-term revenue. These strategies come from roofing companies that have generated $2 million to $8 million in annual storm damage revenue, along with data from insurance industry reports and digital marketing campaigns run at scale.

If you are a roofing contractor, restoration company, or exterior remodeling business looking to systematize your storm response, this is the most detailed playbook available.

Why Storm Damage Lead Generation Is Different

Standard roofing marketing operates on a slow, predictable cycle. A homeowner notices a leak, researches contractors over a week or two, collects three bids, and schedules work. Storm damage compresses that timeline into hours. A homeowner with a tree through their roof or hail damage covering every shingle does not comparison shop. They call the first contractor who shows up.

This urgency creates a unique dynamic. Lead quality is high because the need is immediate and non-discretionary. Close rates are often 40% to 60% for storm damage leads versus 15% to 25% for standard replacement leads. Average job values are higher because insurance companies are paying, not homeowners out of pocket.

But the window is narrow. Most storm damage leads are captured within the first 72 hours after the event. After two weeks, homeowners have already signed with competitors or filed claims with preferred vendor programs. Speed and preparation matter more than brand recognition or even price.

The Economics of Storm Damage Leads

Understanding the numbers helps you allocate budget and set expectations. Here is what roofing companies typically see during active storm seasons:

Metric Storm Damage Lead Standard Roofing Lead
Average cost per lead (PPC) $85 – $250 $120 – $350
Close rate 40% – 60% 15% – 25%
Average job value $12,000 – $25,000 $8,000 – $15,000
Time from lead to contract 1 – 3 days 2 – 6 weeks
Customer acquisition cost $140 – $625 $480 – $2,333

The customer acquisition cost advantage is dramatic. A storm damage lead that costs $150 and closes at 50% produces a customer for $300. A standard lead at the same price with a 20% close rate costs $750 to acquire. That gap explains why roofing companies in hail-prone states like Texas, Colorado, and Minnesota build their entire business model around storm chasing.

Types of Storm Events That Drive Leads

Not all storms generate equal opportunity. Understanding which events produce the most leads helps you prioritize markets and timing:

  • Hail storms: The most profitable event type. Hail damage is often invisible from the ground, so homeowners need inspections. Insurance typically covers full replacement. Hail storms in Texas alone generate over $1 billion in roofing claims annually.
  • Wind storms: High winds lift shingles, tear flashing, and cause tree damage. Claims are common but may be partial rather than full replacement. Wind events are harder to map precisely than hail.
  • Tornadoes: Catastrophic damage with immediate visibility. Leads are abundant but competition is extreme. Often requires out-of-state crews and rapid mobilization.
  • Hurricanes: Massive scale but complex. Requires licensing in multiple states, long-duration campaigns, and significant capital. Best suited for established regional players.
  • Ice dams and winter storms: Seasonal and regional. Less competitive but lower average job values. Strong in northern markets.

Pre-Storm Strategies: Building the Foundation

The contractors who win after a storm are the ones who prepared before it. Pre-storm preparation determines 70% of your post-storm success. Companies that try to spin up campaigns after the event already missed the window.

Establish Insurance Company Relationships

Insurance companies control the flow of storm damage work more than any other factor. Preferred vendor programs, direct repair programs, and adjuster relationships determine which contractors get called first.

Start by identifying the top insurance carriers in your market. State Farm, Allstate, Farmers, USAA, and Liberty Mutual collectively represent over 60% of homeowner policies nationwide. Each has different requirements for contractor networks.

Apply to become a preferred vendor or approved contractor. This typically requires:

  • General liability insurance of at least $1 million
  • Workers compensation coverage
  • State roofing contractor license
  • Clean BBB rating and minimal complaints
  • Willingness to accept insurance pricing (Xactimate rates)
  • Signed contractor network agreements

The application process takes 30 to 90 days. Do not wait for a storm warning. Get approved during the off-season when underwriters have bandwidth to process applications.

Beyond formal programs, build relationships with individual adjusters. Adjusters are overworked during storm season and need reliable contractors who respond quickly, document thoroughly, and do not create complaints. A good adjuster relationship can produce 20 to 50 direct referrals per major event.

Build Your Digital Infrastructure

Your website, landing pages, and ad accounts must be ready to scale instantly. A storm hits and traffic spikes 10x within hours. If your site crashes or your landing page takes three days to build, you lose the entire surge.

Create storm-specific landing pages before season starts. Each page should target a specific storm type and location. Examples:

  • "Hail Damage Roof Repair in Dallas-Fort Worth"
  • "Emergency Roof Tarping in Colorado Springs"
  • "Wind Damage Roof Inspection in Minneapolis"

Each landing page needs specific elements that convert storm traffic:

  • Emergency phone number above the fold, click-to-call on mobile
  • "We work with all insurance companies" trust signal
  • Free inspection offer with same-day or next-day scheduling
  • Photo proof of past storm work (before/after, not stock images)
  • Local address and service area map
  • Insurance claim assistance as a listed service
  • Live chat or instant response form
Landing Page Element Impact on Conversion Rate
Click-to-call phone number +35% mobile conversion
Same-day inspection promise +28% form submission rate
Insurance company logos +18% trust and conversion
Before/after storm photos +22% time on page
Local address visible +15% contact rate

Set Up Storm Tracking and Alert Systems

You cannot respond to storms you do not know about. Set up multiple monitoring systems to catch events as they happen:

  • National Weather Service alerts: Subscribe to severe weather alerts for every market you serve. The NWS issues severe thunderstorm warnings, tornado warnings, and hail alerts in real time.
  • Hail tracking apps: Tools like HailStrike, Interactive Hail Maps, and WeatherOps provide precise hail swath mapping. You can see exactly which neighborhoods received 1-inch, 1.5-inch, or 2-inch hail.
  • NOAA Storm Events Database: Historical data on every reported severe weather event. Use this to identify your market's storm frequency and plan staffing.
  • Social media monitoring: Set up Google Alerts and social listening for "hail [your city]" and "storm damage [your city]." Homeowners post photos within minutes of an event.

HailStrike and similar tools cost $200 to $500 per month but pay for themselves with a single accurate storm identification. A contractor who knows about a hail storm in a specific zip code within two hours can deploy door-knockers and launch geo-targeted ads before competitors even check the weather.

Pre-Position Content and Ad Creative

Write your storm content before the season starts. When a storm hits, you need to publish immediately, not draft blog posts. Prepare the following content library:

  • 5 to 10 blog posts covering different storm types and damage signs
  • 3 to 5 video scripts for emergency response content
  • 20 to 30 social media posts with storm damage photo templates
  • Email sequences for storm-affected homeowner lists
  • Ad copy variations for Google, Facebook, and Nextdoor

For ad creative, prepare image templates with your branding that you can populate with storm-specific photos within an hour. Canva or Figma templates work well. Include your phone number, "Free Inspection," and "We Bill Insurance" on every image.

Train Your Team for Storm Response

Storm mode is different from normal operations. Everyone on your team needs to know their role before the event. Create a storm response playbook that covers:

  • Who monitors weather alerts and makes the call to activate storm mode
  • How to adjust ad budgets and activate pre-built campaigns
  • Who answers phones and how to handle the surge in calls
  • Inspection scheduling protocol for same-day and next-day appointments
  • Crew dispatch procedures for emergency tarping and temporary repairs
  • Documentation requirements for insurance claims
  • Communication with adjusters and insurance companies

Run a tabletop drill before storm season. Simulate a hail storm hitting your primary service area. Walk through every step from alert to first inspection. Identify bottlenecks and fix them before real money is on the line.

During-Storm Strategies: Capturing the Surge

When a severe storm hits your market, you have 24 to 72 hours to capture the majority of leads. Every hour of delay costs you jobs. This section covers the exact actions to take from the moment a storm is confirmed.

Activate Emergency PPC Campaigns

Google Ads is the fastest way to reach storm-damaged homeowners. Within 30 minutes of a storm, homeowners are searching "roof repair after hail," "emergency roof tarping," and "roofing contractor near me." Your ads need to be live before they finish typing.

Set up emergency campaign templates in your Google Ads account before storm season. When a storm hits, duplicate the template, update the location targeting to the affected zip codes, and activate. Your campaigns should include:

  • Emergency keywords: "emergency roof repair," "roof tarping," "storm damage roof," "hail damage repair," "wind damage roof," "tree fell on roof," plus city and zip code modifiers.
  • Negative keywords: "DIY," "how to," "cost to," "cheap," "self" — filter out researchers and keep your budget focused on buyers.
  • Ad copy: Lead with urgency. "24/7 Emergency Roof Repair in [City]. Free Inspection. We Bill Insurance. Call Now." Include call extensions, location extensions, and sitelinks to your storm landing page.
  • Budget: Set daily budgets 5x to 10x your normal spend. Storm traffic is concentrated and temporary. A $200 daily budget becomes $1,000 to $2,000 for 48 to 72 hours.
Ad Platform Best For Typical CPL (Storm) Speed to Launch
Google Search Ads High-intent searches $85 – $180 30 minutes
Google Local Service Ads Local trust, pay per lead $65 – $150 Pre-approved only
Facebook/Instagram Ads Geo-targeted awareness $40 – $90 1 – 2 hours
Nextdoor Ads Neighborhood targeting $50 – $120 2 – 4 hours

Google Local Service Ads deserve special attention. These appear at the very top of search results with a "Google Guaranteed" badge. Homeowners trust them more than standard ads. The catch: you must be background-checked and approved by Google before the storm. Start that process 60 to 90 days before storm season. Once approved, your cost per lead is typically 20% to 40% lower than standard search ads.

Deploy Geo-Targeted Social Media Ads

Facebook and Instagram ads let you target homeowners in the exact neighborhoods that received storm damage. This precision is impossible with traditional media. You can show ads to homeowners on the specific streets where hail was confirmed.

Use hail swath data from HailStrike or Interactive Hail Maps to define your audience. Upload the affected zip codes or draw a radius around the storm path. Layer in homeowner demographics: age 35 to 65, homeowners, income $60k+.

Your creative should be storm-specific. Use actual photos from the event, not stock images. If you have a crew in the area, take photos of damaged roofs and use them in ads within hours. Authenticity converts better than polished marketing during emergencies.

Video ads perform exceptionally well for storm damage. A 15-second video showing your crew tarping a roof, with text overlay "We are in [Neighborhood] today. Free inspections. Call [Number]," generates 2x to 3x the engagement of static images.

Launch Door-to-Door Canvassing

Digital ads capture homeowners who are actively searching. Door-to-door canvassing captures everyone else. The most successful storm damage contractors run both simultaneously.

Canvassing works best when it is immediate and organized. Within 6 to 12 hours of a confirmed hail or wind event, deploy teams to the affected neighborhoods. Each canvasser should have:

  • A mapped territory with specific streets to cover
  • A tablet or phone with a lead capture app (JobNimbus, AccuLynx, or CompanyCam)
  • Branded flyers with your phone number and "Free Storm Damage Inspection"
  • Training on how to identify visible damage from the street
  • A script focused on helping, not selling

The best canvassing script is educational, not pushy. "Hi, I am [Name] with [Company]. We are inspecting homes in this neighborhood after last night's hail storm. Most homeowners cannot see hail damage from the ground, but it voids your roof warranty if not addressed. We offer free inspections with photo documentation for your insurance. Would you like us to take a look?"

Set daily targets. A good canvasser should generate 8 to 15 qualified leads per day in a heavily damaged neighborhood. At a 40% close rate and $15,000 average job, one canvasser produces $48,000 to $90,000 in signed contracts per day.

Activate Emergency Response Content

Content marketing during a storm is about speed and relevance, not perfection. Publish immediately and update as you learn more.

  • Blog post: "What to Do After Last Night's Hail Storm in [City]" — publish within 4 hours. Include photos from the area, steps homeowners should take, and how to file an insurance claim.
  • Social media updates: Post every 2 to 3 hours during the first day. Share photos of damage, crew deployments, and inspection availability. Use local hashtags like #[City]Hail or #[City]Storm.
  • Email to existing list: If you have past customers in the affected area, email them immediately. They already trust you. A simple "We are here to help after today's storm" email with your emergency number generates callbacks.
  • Nextdoor posts: Post in the affected neighborhoods on Nextdoor. Homeowners use this platform heavily during storms to share information and ask for contractor recommendations.

Answer Every Call Within 3 Rings

During storm surges, your phone will ring constantly. Every missed call is a lost job. Homeowners call three contractors and hire the first one who answers. If you send them to voicemail, they have already moved to the next search result.

Options for handling call volume:

  • Overflow call center: Services like Signpost, Smith.ai, or Ruby answer calls 24/7 and book appointments directly into your calendar. Cost is $200 to $600 per month plus per-minute fees.
  • Dedicated storm phone team: Train office staff or hire temporary phone operators during storm season. Pay hourly plus a small bonus per booked inspection.
  • Call routing: Use a service like CallRail to route storm calls to a dedicated line with multiple recipients. All ring simultaneously until someone answers.

Track your answer rate. Aim for 95%+ during storm events. If your answer rate drops below 80%, you are hemorrhaging leads.

Post-Storm Strategies: Converting and Maximizing

The storm has passed. The initial surge of emergency calls slows down. Now the real work begins. Post-storm is where contractors separate themselves. The companies that systematize follow-up, nurture insurance claims, and build referral systems generate 3x to 5x more revenue from the same storm than those who only chase the initial rush.

Follow Up on Every Inspection

Not every inspection results in an immediate contract. Some homeowners need time to process. Others are waiting for their insurance adjuster. A percentage are shopping around. Your follow-up system determines how many of these eventually sign.

Create a structured follow-up sequence for every inspection:

  • Day 0 (immediately after inspection): Send a summary email with photos, damage assessment, and recommended next steps. Include your proposal if applicable.
  • Day 1: Text message checking if they have questions about the inspection.
  • Day 3: Phone call to discuss their insurance claim status and offer to meet the adjuster on site.
  • Day 7: Email with a customer testimonial from a similar storm repair and a reminder of your availability.
  • Day 14: Final phone call. If they have not moved forward, ask directly what is holding them back and address it.

Use a CRM to automate this. JobNimbus, AccuLynx, and Jobber all have automated follow-up sequences. The key is mixing channels: email, text, and phone. Relying on one channel gives homeowners too many chances to ignore you.

Meet Adjusters on Site

This is the single highest-impact action in post-storm roofing. When a homeowner files an insurance claim, the insurance company sends an adjuster to inspect the damage. If you are not there, the adjuster makes decisions without your input. If you are there, you can point out damage, provide documentation, and advocate for full replacement instead of repair.

Train your sales team to attend every adjuster meeting. They should bring:

  • Detailed photo documentation of all damage
  • A written scope of work with line items
  • Knowledge of local building codes that require full replacement
  • Professional demeanor — adjusters are people too, and they respond better to cooperation than confrontation

Contractors who attend adjuster meetings see 25% to 40% higher claim approvals and 15% to 20% higher claim values. A single attended meeting can mean the difference between a $8,000 repair approval and a $18,000 full replacement.

Supplement Claims for Full Value

Initial insurance estimates are often low. Adjusters work from standard pricing databases and may miss code upgrades, overhead and profit, or full scope items. Supplementation is the process of requesting additional funds to cover the true cost of the job.

Common supplement items that adjusters initially omit:

  • Code upgrade requirements (ice and water shield, drip edge, decking replacement)
  • Overhead and profit (10% overhead + 10% profit on jobs with three or more trades)
  • Full decking replacement when damage exceeds 25% of surface area
  • Chimney flashing, skylight replacement, and ventilation upgrades
  • Dump fees, permit costs, and magnet cleanup

Supplementation requires documentation and persistence. Submit a detailed written request with photos, code citations, and line-item pricing. Follow up weekly until resolved. Many contractors hire dedicated supplement specialists or use third-party services like ClaimTek or Supplement Pros. These services charge 10% to 20% of the supplemented amount but often recover $3,000 to $8,000 per claim.

Build a Referral Engine from Storm Jobs

Storm-damaged neighborhoods are tight-knit during recovery. Homeowners talk to neighbors about their contractors, insurance experiences, and results. A single satisfied customer can produce 3 to 5 referrals in the same subdivision.

Systematize referrals from storm work:

  • Neighbor discount: Offer $500 off or a referral bonus for every neighbor who signs. Display yard signs during and after the job.
  • Block party approach: Once you have three or more jobs on the same street, host a brief informational session. Bring a tent, refreshments, and a sample shingle board. Neighbors see your work and trust spreads.
  • Review requests: Ask for Google reviews immediately after job completion. Storm reviews are highly visible and build credibility for the next event.
  • Photo documentation: Take before, during, and after photos of every job. Use them in marketing for the next storm. Real local work converts better than any stock photo.
Referral Strategy Typical Referral Rate Cost per Referral
Yard signs only 5% – 10% $25 – $50
Yard signs + neighbor discount 15% – 25% $100 – $250
Block party + signs + discount 30% – 45% $150 – $400
Google review + follow-up email 8% – 15% $0 – $25

Nurture Leads Who Delayed

Some homeowners wait months to file claims or schedule work. Statutes of limitations for storm damage claims vary by state but are often 1 to 2 years. A lead who did not convert in week one may convert in month six.

Keep these leads warm with a long-term nurture sequence:

  • Monthly email with storm damage education and customer stories
  • Quarterly check-in call to see if they have filed their claim
  • Seasonal reminders about claim deadlines
  • Retargeting ads on Facebook and Google to stay visible

A roofing company in Oklahoma City maintained a nurture list of 2,400 unconverted storm leads from a 2023 hail event. Over 18 months, 340 of those leads (14%) eventually converted, producing $4.2 million in additional revenue from a single storm.

Ongoing Strategies: Building a Storm Damage Machine

One-time storm success is luck. Repeatable storm success is a system. The contractors who dominate storm markets year after year have built machines that activate automatically and improve with every event.

Develop a Storm Chasing Capability

Storm chasing means traveling to affected areas outside your home market. It is controversial in the roofing industry but highly profitable when done correctly. The key is professionalism and compliance.

Before chasing storms, establish:

  • Licensing: Obtain contractor licenses in target states before storm season. Texas, Colorado, Minnesota, and Florida have specific requirements. Some states require a local business entity or qualifying party.
  • Local partnerships: Partner with a licensed local contractor who provides the legal entity while you provide the sales and installation capacity. This is common and reduces licensing complexity.
  • Logistics: Pre-arrange hotel blocks, equipment storage, and material suppliers in chase markets. After a major event, hotel rooms within 100 miles sell out in hours.
  • Crew housing: Rent houses or apartments for crews rather than hotel rooms. It is cheaper, more stable, and keeps crews together for months at a time.

Storm chasing requires capital. You are paying for travel, lodging, and payroll before any revenue comes in. Most chase operations need $50,000 to $150,000 in working capital per event. The returns can be substantial — established chase crews generate $500,000 to $2 million per major storm — but the risk is real. Do not chase storms until your home market operation is profitable and stable.

Build a Database of Storm-Affected Homes

Every storm produces data. Smart contractors capture and organize it. Your storm database becomes a competitive asset that improves with every event.

Track the following for every storm:

  • Exact date, time, and storm type
  • Hail size, wind speed, and affected zip codes
  • Number of inspections performed
  • Number of contracts signed and total value
  • Insurance companies involved and approval rates
  • Neighborhoods with highest conversion rates
  • Canvasser performance by territory
  • Lead source performance (Google, Facebook, canvassing, referrals)

Over time, this data reveals patterns. You learn which neighborhoods convert best, which insurance companies pay fairly, which lead sources produce the highest ROI, and which salespeople close storm leads most effectively. These insights let you allocate resources more precisely with every subsequent storm.

Invest in Local SEO for Storm Terms

Paid ads capture immediate demand. SEO captures long-term demand. Homeowners search storm-related terms for months after an event. If your website ranks organically for "hail damage roof repair [city]," you get free leads long after you have stopped paying for ads.

Target these storm-related SEO keywords:

  • "[City] hail damage roof repair"
  • "roof inspection after storm [city]"
  • "how to file roof insurance claim [state]"
  • "emergency roof tarping [city]"
  • "wind damage roof signs"
  • "hail damage roof [city] [year]"

Create dedicated pages for major storms after they occur. A page titled "March 2026 Hail Storm Damage in Dallas: What Homeowners Need to Know" ranks well for months and establishes you as the local authority. Include photos from the actual storm, damage statistics, and your company's response. These pages attract backlinks from local news and community forums.

Join and Lead Industry Associations

Industry associations provide credibility, networking, and early information. The National Roofing Contractors Association (NRCA), regional roofing associations, and storm-specific groups like the United Hail Association connect you with adjusters, suppliers, and other contractors.

Active participation matters more than membership. Volunteer for committees, speak at events, and contribute to industry publications. When adjusters and insurance professionals recognize your name, you get preferential treatment during storm events.

Automate and Systematize Everything

Manual processes break under storm volume. Automation ensures consistency when you are processing 50 inspections per day instead of five.

Systems to automate:

  • Lead intake: Web forms, phone calls, and canvassing apps should feed directly into your CRM. No manual data entry.
  • Appointment scheduling: Use Calendly, Acuity, or your CRM's scheduling tool to let homeowners book inspections online. Reduce phone tag.
  • Document generation: Auto-populate proposals, contracts, and insurance paperwork from CRM data. Tools like DocuSign and PandaDoc integrate with most roofing CRMs.
  • Follow-up sequences: Trigger email and text sequences based on inspection status, claim status, and job phase.
  • Review requests: Automatically send review requests 3 days after job completion. Include a direct link to your Google Business Profile.

A roofing company in Denver automated their entire storm workflow using JobNimbus, Zapier, and Twilio. When a hail alert triggered, their system automatically increased Google Ads budgets, sent notification texts to the sales team, posted to social media, and added affected zip codes to Facebook ad audiences. Response time dropped from 4 hours to 15 minutes. Storm revenue increased 180% year over year with the same team size.

Prepare everything you will publish when storms hit.

Frequently Asked Questions

How quickly should I launch ads after a storm?

Within 1 to 2 hours for digital ads. Homeowners start searching immediately. Google Ads can be live in 30 minutes if you have pre-built campaign templates. Facebook ads take 1 to 2 hours for approval. The first 6 to 12 hours capture the highest-intent leads.

What is the best lead source for storm damage?

Google Search Ads and Google Local Service Ads produce the highest-intent leads with the best close rates. Canvassing produces the highest volume but requires trained teams. Facebook and Nextdoor are effective for awareness but convert at lower rates. The best contractors use all four simultaneously.

How much should I budget for storm season PPC?

Budget $5,000 to $15,000 per month during active storm season for a single market. When a storm hits, increase daily budgets 5x to 10x for 48 to 72 hours. A major event can consume $10,000 to $30,000 in ad spend in a week. Set monthly caps to prevent overspend during slow periods.

Do I need a special license for storm chasing?

Yes. Every state has its own contractor licensing requirements. Some require a local business entity, passing an exam, or a qualifying party with state-specific credentials. Research requirements 90 days before chasing. Operating without proper licensing exposes you to fines, job shutdowns, and liability issues.

How do I find out exactly where hail hit?

Use hail tracking services like HailStrike, Interactive Hail Maps, or WeatherOps. These tools show precise hail swaths with size measurements. NOAA also publishes storm reports, but with less precision. Local news and social media confirm ground-level impact within hours.

Should I meet the insurance adjuster on every job?

Yes, whenever possible. Contractors who attend adjuster meetings see 25% to 40% higher claim approvals and 15% to 20% higher claim values. Your presence ensures all damage is documented and code requirements are considered. Schedule adjuster meetings when you schedule the inspection.

What is the statute of limitations for storm damage claims?

It varies by state, typically 1 to 2 years from the date of loss. Some states allow longer for hidden damage. Homeowners can file claims months after the storm. Maintain your nurture sequences for at least 12 months after every major event.

How do I handle the surge in phone calls?

Use a combination of call routing, overflow answering services, and dedicated storm phone staff. Aim for a 95%+ answer rate during events. Services like Smith.ai, Ruby, or Signpost answer calls 24/7 and book directly into your calendar. Every missed call is a lost job.

What should my door-to-door canvassers say?

Lead with education, not sales. "We are inspecting homes in this neighborhood after last night's hail. Most homeowners cannot see hail damage from the ground, but it can void your warranty. We offer free inspections with photo documentation for your insurance." Avoid pressure. Offer value. Respect "no."

How do I supplement low insurance estimates?

Submit a detailed written request with photos, code citations, and line-item pricing. Common missed items include code upgrades, overhead and profit, full decking replacement, and accessory items. Follow up weekly. Consider hiring a supplement specialist or service if volume justifies it.

Is storm chasing worth it for a small roofing company?

Not initially. Build a profitable home market operation first. Storm chasing requires $50,000 to $150,000 in working capital, multi-state licensing, and crew logistics. Start by dominating your local storm market. Once you have systems and capital, expand to chase markets methodically.

How long does storm damage SEO take to work?

3 to 6 months for new pages to rank. That is why you start before storm season. Create storm-specific pages during the off-season so they have time to build authority. After a storm, publish event-specific content immediately to capture news and social sharing signals.

What CRM is best for storm damage roofing?

JobNimbus, AccuLynx, and Jobber are the most popular. JobNimbus excels at automation and integrations. AccuLynx has strong production management. Jobber is simpler and more affordable. All three handle storm workflows well. Choose based on your team size and complexity needs.

How do I prevent storm leads from going cold?

Multi-channel follow-up: email, text, and phone. Automate sequences in your CRM triggered by inspection date. Offer value in every touch: claim filing tips, adjuster meeting prep, deadline reminders. Do not give up for at least 60 days. Many homeowners delay decisions but eventually convert with consistent follow-up.

What is the biggest mistake roofing companies make with storm leads?

Waiting too long to respond. The contractors who capture storm leads act within hours, not days. They have pre-built systems, trained teams, and immediate deployment capability. The second biggest mistake is poor follow-up — signing the initial rush but losing the majority of leads to competitors who nurture better.

Storm damage lead generation is not about luck or timing. It is about preparation and systems. The roofing companies that generate millions in storm revenue every year have built machines that activate automatically, scale instantly, and improve continuously.

Your 90-day preparation timeline starts today. Build your landing pages. Set up your ad accounts. Train your team. Create your content library. Automate your follow-up. When the next storm hits your market, you will be ready to capture every lead that matters while your competitors are still checking the weather.

The economics are clear. A single well-prepared storm season can produce more revenue than a full year of standard roofing marketing. The customer acquisition costs are lower, the job values are higher, and the close rates are better. The only question is whether you will be ready.
